rules.diagnosis: Package '{package_name}' contains no ML-related code (CCPP = {ccpp_score:.2f}). This package appears to be pure utility/infrastructure code with no pipeline functionality detected.
rules.recommendation: ACTION REQUIRED: Rename this package to clearly indicate its non-ML purpose (e.g., 'utils/', 'common/', 'helpers/', or 'infrastructure/'). Move it outside the main ML pipeline directory structure to avoid confusion and improve project organization.

rules.diagnosis: Package '{package_name}' has unusual structure (CCPP = {ccpp_score:.2f}). Multiple stages detected but no phase classification, indicating potential misclassification or mixed utility code.
rules.recommendation: REVIEW NEEDED: This pattern is uncommon. Verify that FPC analysis is correctly identifying ML content. If this is utility code, consolidate into a single utilities package. If it contains ML code, ensure proper phase detection is working.

rules.diagnosis: Package '{package_name}' shows phase/stage detection without ML content (CCPP = {ccpp_score:.2f}). This indicates a potential analysis anomaly.
rules.recommendation: INVESTIGATION REQUIRED: Review this package manually. This pattern suggests either: (1) misclassification of utility code, (2) incomplete FPC analysis, or (3) abstract base classes. Consider refactoring if this is utility code.

rules.diagnosis: Package '{package_name}' has ML content with phase classification but no stage detection (CCPP = {ccpp_score:.2f}). This may indicate abstract or incomplete pipeline code.
rules.recommendation: VERIFY: Check if this package contains abstract base classes, interfaces, or incomplete implementations. If it's concrete pipeline code, review why stage detection failed. Consider adding proper pipeline stage indicators.

rules.diagnosis: Very Low Cohesion  The {package_name} package includes several ML phases and non-ML content and some stages are split in several modules.
rules.recommendation: Separate non_ML content and reorganize. Move non-ML content to another non_ML package. Consider to create subpackages by stage (data_cleaning, feature_engineering, etc.) if the number of modules for stage is or grows too large.

rules.diagnosis: Low Cohesion  The {package_name} package includes several ML phases and non-ML content.
rules.recommendation: Separate non_ML content. Move non-ML content to another non_ML package.

rules.diagnosis: High Cohesion The {package_name} package includes several ML phases, all related to the pipeline, and each stage has its own module.
rules.recommendation: Mantain structure. Consolidate the structure and consider to create subpackages by stage (data_cleaning, feature_engineering, etc.) if the number of modules for stage grows too large.

rules.diagnosis: Medium Cohesion The {package_name} package includes several ML phases, all related to the pipeline, but some stages are split in several modules.
rules.recommendation: Group by ML phase. Consolidate modules or subpackages of the same phase in one subpackage. Maintain hierarchy if already organized by phase. Consider to create subpackages by stage (data_cleaning, feature_engineering, etc.) if the number of modules for stage is or grows too large.

rules.diagnosis: Medium Cohesion The {package_name} package belongs to a single ML phase but includes non-ML elements.
rules.recommendation: Separate non-ML content. Move non-ML content to another non_ML package. For large packages, consider to create subpackages by stage (data_cleaning, feature_engineering, etc.).

rules.diagnosis: High Cohesion The package covers multiple ML stages within one phase.
rules.recommendation: Maintain structure. Ensure each stage has its own module or subpackage. Split or merge only to balance size and clarity.

rules.diagnosis: Medium Cohesion The package focuses on one ML stage but includes some unrelated code.
rules.recommendation: Keep ML stage isolated and move non-ML code to another non-ML package or reuse existing subpackages if available.

rules.diagnosis: Very High Cohesion  The package (and its subpackages) focuses exclusively on one ML stage of one phase.
rules.recommendation: Maintain and document as a reference model for future pipeline designs.
